newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan bank to keep loose policy on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan bank to keep loose policy on stock rally.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank would keep its "stable-to-loose, but not-too-loose" monetary policy despite a recent stock market rally, a central bank official on Thursday quoted central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong as saying.

"At a time when stock market or property market prices surge, as long as they do not affect consumer price stability, the central bank has no need to adjust its monetary policy," the official quoted Sheu as telling reporters late on Wednesday at the airport when he returned from a foreign visit.
"The stock market rally occurred in the last few days, and the market will automatically adjust to the short-term price changes by itself," Sheu was quoted as saying.

"Currently, domestic consumer prices are at pretty low levels. The central bank will closely watch the stock market movements, but our stable-to-loose, but not-to-loose money policy will remain unchanged," Sheu said.
"But if stock market or property market price surges show a long-term trend and threaten consumer price stability, the central bank will make some adjustment to its monetary policy," he said.
Sheu made the comments after the stock index surged for five straight sessions and on Wednesday hit a seven-year closing high of 8,713.49 points.
After weeks of modest volume, Wednesday's turnover surged to an extremely heavy T$207.4 billion, the highest level since the market hit an all-time high of T$238.9 billion on April 8.
Sheu was quoted as saying the stock market rally reflected the improving domestic economic outlook, but the central bank hoped the stock market would not rally too sharply.
Taiwan's consumer prices grew an average 1.27 percent year-on-year in the first five months, a nine-year-low and much lower than the government's target of 3.0 percent growth for 1997.
